36:class CommandHandler(BaseHandler[Update, CCT, RT]):
37:    """Handler class to handle Telegram commands.
38:
39:    Commands are Telegram messages that start with a :attr:`telegram.MessageEntity.BOT_COMMAND`
40:    (so with ``/``, optionally followed by an ``@`` and the bot's name and/or some additional
41:    text). The handler will add a :obj:`list` to the :class:`CallbackContext` named
42:    :attr:`CallbackContext.args`. It will contain a list of strings, which is the text following
43:    the command split on single or consecutive whitespace characters.
44:
45:    By default, the handler listens to messages as well as edited messages. To change this behavior
46:    use :attr:`~filters.UpdateType.EDITED_MESSAGE <telegram.ext.filters.UpdateType.EDITED_MESSAGE>`
47:    in the filter argument.
48:
49:    Note:
50:        :class:`CommandHandler` does *not* handle (edited) channel posts and does *not* handle
51:        commands that are part of a caption. Please use :class:`~telegram.ext.MessageHandler`
52:        with a suitable combination of filters (e.g.
53:        :attr:`telegram.ext.filters.UpdateType.CHANNEL_POSTS`,
54:        :attr:`telegram.ext.filters.CAPTION` and :class:`telegram.ext.filters.Regex`) to handle
55:        those messages.
56:
57:    Note:
58:        If you want to support a different entity in the beginning, e.g. if a command message is
59:        wrapped in a :attr:`telegram.MessageEntity.CODE`, use the
60:        :class:`telegram.ext.PrefixHandler`.
61:
62:    Warning:
63:        When setting :paramref:`block` to :obj:`False`, you cannot rely on adding custom
64:        attributes to :class:`telegram.ext.CallbackContext`. See its docs for more info.
65:
66:    Examples:
67:        * :any:`Timer Bot <examples.timerbot>`
68:        * :any:`Error Handler Bot <examples.errorhandlerbot>`
69:
70:    .. versionchanged:: 20.0
71:
72:        * Renamed the attribute ``command`` to :attr:`commands`, which now is always a
73:          :class:`frozenset`
74:        * Updating the commands this handler listens to is no longer possible.
75:
76:    Args:
77:        command (:obj:`str` | Collection[:obj:`str`]):
78:            The command or list of commands this handler should listen for. Case-insensitive.
79:            Limitations are the same as for :attr:`telegram.BotCommand.command`.
80:        callback (:term:`coroutine function`): The callback function for this handler. Will be
81:            called when :meth:`check_update` has determined that an update should be processed by
82:            this handler. Callback signature::
83:
84:                async def callback(update: Update, context: CallbackContext)
85:
86:            The return value of the callback is usually ignored except for the special case of
87:            :class:`telegram.ext.ConversationHandler`.
88:        filters (:class:`telegram.ext.filters.BaseFilter`, optional): A filter inheriting from
89:            :class:`telegram.ext.filters.BaseFilter`. Standard filters can be found in
90:            :mod:`telegram.ext.filters`. Filters can be combined using bitwise
91:            operators (``&`` for :keyword:`and`, ``|`` for :keyword:`or`, ``~`` for :keyword:`not`)
92:        block (:obj:`bool`, optional): Determines whether the return value of the callback should
93:            be awaited before processing the next handler in
94:            :meth:`telegram.ext.Application.process_update`. Defaults to :obj:`True`.
95:
96:            .. seealso:: :wiki:`Concurrency`
97:        has_args (:obj:`bool` | :obj:`int`, optional):
98:            Determines whether the command handler should process the update or not.
99:            If :obj:`True`, the handler will process any non-zero number of args.
100:            If :obj:`False`, the handler will only process if there are no args.
101:            if :obj:`int`, the handler will only process if there are exactly that many args.
102:            Defaults to :obj:`None`, which means the handler will process any or no args.
103:
104:            .. versionadded:: 20.5
105:
106:    Raises:
107:        :exc:`ValueError`: When the command is too long or has illegal chars.
108:
109:    Attributes:
110:        commands (frozenset[:obj:`str`]): The set of commands this handler should listen for.
111:        callback (:term:`coroutine function`): The callback function for this handler.
112:        filters (:class:`telegram.ext.filters.BaseFilter`): Optional. Only allow updates with these
113:            filters.
114:        block (:obj:`bool`): Determines whether the return value of the callback should be
115:            awaited before processing the next handler in
116:            :meth:`telegram.ext.Application.process_update`.
117:        has_args (:obj:`bool` | :obj:`int` | None):
118:            Optional argument, otherwise all implementations of :class:`CommandHandler` will break.
119:            Defaults to :obj:`None`, which means the handler will process any args or no args.
120:
121:            .. versionadded:: 20.5
122:    """
123:
124:    __slots__ = ("commands", "filters", "has_args")
125:
126:    def __init__(
127:        self: "CommandHandler[CCT, RT]",
128:        command: SCT[str],
129:        callback: HandlerCallback[Update, CCT, RT],
130:        filters: Optional[filters_module.BaseFilter] = None,
131:        block: DVType[bool] = DEFAULT_TRUE,
132:        has_args: Optional[Union[bool, int]] = None,
133:    ):
134:        super().__init__(callback, block=block)
135:
136:        if isinstance(command, str):
137:            commands = frozenset({command.lower()})
138:        else:
139:            commands = frozenset(x.lower() for x in command)
140:        for comm in commands:
141:            if not re.match(r"^[\da-z_]{1,32}$", comm):
142:                raise ValueError(f"Command `{comm}` is not a valid bot command")
143:        self.commands: frozenset[str] = commands
144:
145:        self.filters: filters_module.BaseFilter = (
146:            filters if filters is not None else filters_module.UpdateType.MESSAGES
147:        )
148:
149:        self.has_args: Optional[Union[bool, int]] = has_args
150:
151:        if (isinstance(self.has_args, int)) and (self.has_args < 0):
152:            raise ValueError("CommandHandler argument has_args cannot be a negative integer")
153:
154:    def _check_correct_args(self, args: list[str]) -> Optional[bool]:
155:        """Determines whether the args are correct for this handler. Implemented in check_update().
156:        Args:
157:            args (:obj:`list`): The args for the handler.
158:        Returns:
159:            :obj:`bool`: Whether the args are valid for this handler.
160:        """
161:        return bool(
162:            (self.has_args is None)
163:            or (self.has_args is True and args)
164:            or (self.has_args is False and not args)
165:            or (isinstance(self.has_args, int) and len(args) == self.has_args)
166:        )

168:    def check_update(
169:        self, update: object
170:    ) -> Optional[Union[bool, tuple[list[str], Optional[Union[bool, FilterDataDict]]]]]:
171:        """Determines whether an update should be passed to this handler's :attr:`callback`.
172:
173:        Args:
174:            update (:class:`telegram.Update` | :obj:`object`): Incoming update.
175:
176:        Returns:
177:            :obj:`list`: The list of args for the handler.
178:
179:        """
180:        if isinstance(update, Update) and update.effective_message:
181:            message = update.effective_message
182:
183:            if (
184:                message.entities
185:                and message.entities[0].type == MessageEntity.BOT_COMMAND
186:                and message.entities[0].offset == 0
187:                and message.text
188:                and message.get_bot()
189:            ):
190:                command = message.text[1 : message.entities[0].length]
191:                args = message.text.split()[1:]
192:                command_parts = command.split("@")
193:                command_parts.append(message.get_bot().username)
194:
195:                if not (
196:                    command_parts[0].lower() in self.commands
197:                    and command_parts[1].lower() == message.get_bot().username.lower()
198:                ):
199:                    return None
200:
201:                if not self._check_correct_args(args):
202:                    return None
203:
204:                filter_result = self.filters.check_update(update)
205:                if filter_result:
206:                    return args, filter_result
207:                return False
208:        return None

210:    def collect_additional_context(
211:        self,
212:        context: CCT,
213:        update: Update,  # noqa: ARG002
214:        application: "Application[Any, CCT, Any, Any, Any, Any]",  # noqa: ARG002
215:        check_result: Optional[Union[bool, tuple[list[str], Optional[bool]]]],
216:    ) -> None:
217:        """Add text after the command to :attr:`CallbackContext.args` as list, split on single
218:        whitespaces and add output of data filters to :attr:`CallbackContext` as well.
219:        """
220:        if isinstance(check_result, tuple):
221:            context.args = check_result[0]
222:            if isinstance(check_result[1], dict):
223:                context.update(check_result[1])"}

I have the needed code and test setup to compute the two compared strings. DONE_WITH_FILE_READING
The test builds a message whose command token is `"/Start@WrongBot"` and sets the bot on that message to `_DummyBot("qa_bot")`. In `CommandHandler.check_update`, `command = message.text[1 : message.entities[0].length]` removes the leading slash and yields `Start@WrongBot`, then `command_parts = command.split("@")` makes `["Start", "WrongBot"]`, and `command_parts.append(message.get_bot().username)` appends `"qa_bot"`. So at the condition, `command_parts[1].lower()` is `"wrongbot"` and `message.get_bot().username.lower()` is `"qa_bot"`.

## Answer
{"condition_values":["wrongbot","qa_bot"]}
